soap.subjective: 58-year-old female presents with 6 months of right knee pain, worse with morning stiffness lasting ~20 minutes and after prolonged sitting. Reports swelling after prolonged walking and crepitus on knee flexion. No trauma. BMI 32. Family history of knee problems. No joint locking.
soap.objective: BMI 32. Periarticular swelling of right knee. ROM 5-110 degrees with pain at end range. Crepitus on passive flexion. Medial joint line tenderness. No ligamentous laxity. X-ray: moderate medial joint space narrowing, osteophyte formation, subchondral sclerosis.

assessment.summary: Moderate right knee osteoarthritis based on clinical presentation and X-ray findings. Risk factors include obesity and family history.

plan.instructions: Physical therapy for quadriceps strengthening. Weight loss counseling. Corticosteroid injection consideration if inadequate response to naproxen. Acetaminophen max 3g/day.
plan.follow_up: 6 weeks to reassess pain control and discuss injection therapy
